text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — planning production deploy: tenant_id column type change (INT -> UUID) + incremental backfill. Tentative window: Friday 2025-04-11 02:00 UTC. Expect small per-shard jobs and a short lock during the swap. Follow the rollout steps below and ack if you need a different window.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled by alex.chen for 2025-04-11T02:00:00Z. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenantid-swap (pin: v2.3.1).

Priya Singh: Can you clarify the lock surface? Is this an exclusive table-level DDL or row-level swap?

Alex Chen: It's a fast ALTER TYPE for the shadow column + atomic swap using view/table rename. There will be a brief exclusive lock on the target table for the final rename (~5-15s per shard). Backfill runs beforehand to populate shadow_uuid where needed.

Josh Patel: For safety, propose we run a canary on 3 small tenants first, then expand to 20% traffic, then full. Also add a toggle (feature flag) to serve old id form for 5m if we need to rollback.

Maya Rodriguez: Rollback plan: if the rename fails or locks exceed threshold, we abort and run rollback script to restore previous table names and metrics. Need DB + deploy approval to force abort. Add step to revert routing rule in API gateway.

Sam (DBA): Backfill SQL (dry-run):
```sql
BEGIN;
-- populate shadow_uuid for rows missing it
UPDATE tenant_table SET shadow_uuid = gen_random_uuid() WHERE shadow_uuid IS NULL LIMIT 10000;
-- verify FK integrity and counts
COMMIT;
```
We'll run smaller batches with a 10s sleep between batches.

Lina (SRE): Ops checklist:
- Preflight: run fk counts and row-estimates (script linked in runbook)
- Quiesce signal: set deployment_quiesce=true to pause heavy background jobs 10m before swap
- Alerting: set PagerDuty if lock > 60s or replica lag > 30s
- Post-check: tail error logs for 10m and validate critical endpoints

Priya Singh: How are we pinning versions? The app change that parses UUIDs is in release v2025.04.08. We should pin the worker and API images to that tag during the window.

Alex Chen: Agreed. We'll pin API and workers to v2025.04.08 and rollback to v2025.03.30 if we need to revert. I'll add the pinned tags to the release note.

eng-oncall: Confirming maintenance window is OK. We'll mark the Friday 02:00–03:00 UTC slot and mute noisy alerts except high-severity. Anyone needing a different timezone handoff, ping me.

Priya Singh: One more: can we set a short holdpoint after canary expansion to validate metrics (error rate, p95 latency, db locks)? Would prefer 15m stop.

Josh Patel: +1 to 15m holdpoint. Add guardrail: if error rate > 1% or p95 latency > 200ms, abort.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started by alex.chen. Targets: tenants [alpha, beta, gamma]. Canary timeout: 15m.

Alex Chen: Thanks — I'll post the final preflight checklist tomorrow including the exact shard list and the SQL verification queries. Please react with :thumbsup: to acknowledge.

Maya Rodriguez: :thumbsup:

Sam (DBA): :thumbsup: I'll prepare rollback scripts and a step-by-step DB restore plan (logical copy + rename).

Lina (SRE): Noted. I'll create temporary dashboards for the window and ensure the paging rule is set.

Priya Singh: Acknowledged. Will pin versions and schedule health-check smoke tests after canary.

Alex Chen: Final note — release notes draft: https://redwood.internal/releases/2025-04-tenantid-swap (please add any customer-facing caveats).

eng-oncall: If anything changes during the run, use this thread and tag @eng-oncall + @deploy-bot to trigger escalation.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished for tenants [alpha, beta, gamma] — canary succeeded. Moving to 20% expansion.

Josh Patel: Seeing one 65s lock in shard-7 during expand — keeping an eye. If it crosses 90s, trigger abort.

Sam (DBA): I'm watching replication lag, currently 2s.

Alex Chen: Proceeding with remaining shards, holdpoint at 20% for 15m.

deploy-bot: Expansion to 100% complete. Post-check running.

Lina (SRE): Post-checks good. No elevated errors in 10m window. Latency stable.

Maya Rodriguez: Rolling release notes and tagging support. Great job team.

Alex Chen: Closing thread — thanks all.
